newsitem.title: USA: Dollar fears keep IBM out of high-tech rally.
newsitem.headline: Dollar fears keep IBM out of high-tech rally.

text.p: Fears that a strong dollar would clip International Business Machines Corp's 1997 profits kept IBM out of a wave of buying that hit technology stocks and sent Nasdaq surging more than one percent.

IBM shares fell in early trading by almost two points to 143 after three brokerage firms -- Merrill Lynch & Co Inc, Morgan Stanley Group Inc and Salomon Brothers -- on Wednesday cut 1997 profit estimates, citing a strong dollar.

The stock pared most of its losses and was off 1/2 in midday trading. Earlier, bargain hunting had sent the stock up 3/4, but an analyst said the gain was thin compared with the action in other tech stocks -- sparked after Applied Materials Inc posted strong first quarter earnings.

Several industry analysts raised ratings and price targets on Applied Materials, triggering a rally in the semiconductor equipment industry and in the broader technology sector. The Nasdaq Composite jumped 15.9 to 1347.41, or 1.19 percent.
The rally comes on the heels of a sell-off in technology stocks. The Nasdaq has closed lower in six of the last seven sessions.
But as the dollar continued climbing, IBM was left out in the cold, even as the Dow Industrials surged nearly 55 points to 6912 and hit a new intraday high.

Salomon's John Jones wrote "Over the past 45 days, the U.S. dollar has been much stronger ... than our original forecast for 1997 ... We currently see an impact of eight to nine percent on every dollar of international revenue."

Tom Carpenter, chief economist for ASB Capital Management Inc, said multinationals with operations in Europe and Japan will be hit by the "double whammy" of stagnating economies there and currency appreciation in the United States. He added that going forward, there is currently little on a fundamental basis to halt the dollar's rise.
The dollar was just below 124 yen and 1.6860 marks in early afternoon trading.
